verified.exploit_entry_point: The HTTP resource API handlers of package http, served through the product's own handle() wrapper with a real bolt storage backend, a real settings key and a signed JWT for a user whose scope is /user. Filesystem scoping is built by the product's user-loading path (users.Clean), so the BasePathFs scoping is the production one. Security and functional tests drive resourcePostHandler, tusPostHandler, resourcePatchHandler and resourceGetRecursiveHandler directly, which are the handlers the router mounts.
sites: files/file.go:186-228 (WithinScope: existence-based resolution admits a dangling link whose target escapes, and lexical '..' after a symlinked component)
http/resource.go:128-135 (directory creation POST, no containment check)
fileutils/dir.go:31,46-56 and fileutils/file.go:53-59,76 (copy destination tree and per-child destinations, source-only check)
http/resource.go:405-448 (recursive listing root and emitted entries, no containment check)
routes: T1: upload (POST with override) and resumable upload creation through a symlink inside the scope whose target is outside it, absolute, relative, or through a symlinked component before a '..'
T3: directory creation POST under an existing symlinked directory that points outside the scope
T4: copy into a destination tree whose child is an escaping symlink named like a source child, with override
T5: recursive listing rooted below a symlinked directory that points outside the scope
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./files ./fileutils ./http -count=1 (pinned, oracle, alternative, hardening and every check patch that must keep functional green)

traps.shape: the shared containment predicate must decide where a write would really land: a dangling link's target (absolute or relative), further links, and a '..' that applies after a symlinked component, while brand-new files and links that resolve inside the scope keep working
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is one dangling link, so a single link read plus a lexical prefix check looks complete; the pinned comment itself says a dangling link resolves to its parent and is therefore allowed
traps.realistic_because: published fix site; the resolver shape and the in-scope-link keep-working cases are the reader's T1/T2

traps.shape: directory creation on POST never consulted the containment rule; a directory link that already points outside the scope lets the request create a directory outside
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it only creates an empty directory, and the report is about a dangling link that creates a file; the escaping link here already exists and does not dangle
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the POST directory branch reaches MkdirAll with no containment check, and both published fix commits leave the branch as it is

traps.shape: a copy checks the source and the top-level destination, but each child destination is built lexically; an escaping link inside the destination tree is followed when the child is opened or created
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the handler already checks the top-level destination and the copy helpers already run the containment rule, so the destination looks covered
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the per-child destination is built with filepath.Join and opened without a containment check in both published fix commits

traps.shape: the recursive listing walks the raw path and emits every entry it finds; rooted below a symlinked directory that points outside, it discloses out-of-scope names, sizes and times
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it returns only names, sizes and mtimes with no content, and the report is about writes
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the walk is rooted at the request path and only consults the user's access rules, untouched by both published fix commits

patch_checks.why: blind fix produced by run_blindfix after the first gate

wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or request directions exist on this surface
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: paths are resolved by the filesystem itself, so there is no separate spelling parser a malformed identity could fool
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: containment is decided from the filesystem, with no authority, role or secret lookup that could fail open
